source: STEER Project (Save the Children, iDE Cambodia, and the Cambodian Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries) - "Guide on Banana Cultivation Techniques" (សៀវភៅណែនាំស្តីអំពី បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះដំណាំចេក), February 2020
text:
Once seedlings have hardened off in nursery bags (see the propagation entry), they are transplanted into the field. Planting holes are dug roughly 30 to 50 centimeters wide and deep, following the site's row spacing plan (2.5-3 m x 2.5-3 m for a main crop, or roughly 3 x 8 m where banana is used as a shade/nurse crop).

Compost or well-rotted manure is mixed into the excavated soil before the seedling is set in the hole, planted so the top of the root ball sits slightly below the surrounding soil surface, then firmed in and watered. Planting is best done with care to avoid damaging the young root system, since transplant shock can delay establishment.
